items.label: text
items.text: The equation for the reaction to form sulfur trioxide from sulfur dioxide and oxygen is:

items.label: formula
items.text: SO₂(g) + ½O₂(g) ⇌ SO₃(g)   ΔS°_total = 238.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate a value for the equilibrium constant, K, for this reaction (R = 8.31J mol-1 K-1).

items.label: list_item
items.text: K=eStotal/R

items.label: text
items.text: To solve this calculation,press thee*or ebutton onyour calculator.Then enter 238.3÷8.31followed by the equalsbutton.The answer will be displayed.

items.label: text
items.text: Thereisnofirmruleabouttherelationshipbetweentheequilibriumconstant,K,andthepositionof equilibrium of thereaction.

items.label: text
items.text: However, as a general rule we can say that a very large value of K suggests that the position of equilibrium is well over to the products side (i.e. the right-hand side of the equation).

items.label: text
items.text: Similarly, avery small value ofK suggests that theposition of equilibrium iswell overto the reactants side(i.e.theleft-hand side of the equation).
